identity.title: A deep search for large complex organic species toward IRAS16293-2422 B at 3 mm with ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: This paper uses the data of IRAS16293 B taken with ALMA in Band 3 (project code: 2017.1.00518.S; PI: E. F. van Dishoeck).

coordinates.value: 0.5'' offset position from B continuum peak: RA 16h32m22.58s, Dec -24d28m32.8s (J2000)

evidence.quote: $\alpha_{\rm J2000} = 16^{\rm h} 32^{\rm m} 22^{\rm s}.58$ and $\delta_{J2000} = -24^{\circ} 28\ensuremath{'} 32.8\ensuremath{''}$

question.value: Can large complex organic molecules (>8 atoms; e.g. glycerol, propanols) be detected in the deep ALMA Band 3 spectrum of IRAS16293 B, and do column densities and ratios to methanol differ from Band 7 (PILS) because of dust optical depth?

evidence.quote: We aim to search for large molecules ($> 8$ atoms) in the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) Band 3 spectrum of IRAS 16293-2422 B.
taken with ALMA in Band 3 (project code: 2017.1.00518.S; PI: E. F. van Dishoeck)

bands.value: Band 3 (~100 GHz); PILS Band 7 (~345 GHz) for comparison

evidence.quote: This paper uses the data of IRAS16293 B taken with ALMA in Band 3
The frequency ranges covered were ${\sim}90.59-91.41$ GHz (continuum), ${\sim}93.14-93.20$ GHz and ${\sim}103.28-103.52$ GHz.
The spectral resolution was 0.805 km s$^{-1}$, 0.049 km s$^{-1}$, and 0.088 km s$^{-1}$.
We used the data with configuration C43-4
The data have an angular resolution of ${\sim} 0.9\ensuremath{''} \times 0.7\ensuremath{''}$

sensitivity.value: rms ~0.1 K, ~0.3 K and 0.2 K per spectral window (brightness temperature)

evidence.quote: the rms found from line-free regions in each spectral window is ${\sim}0.1$ K, ${\sim}0.3$ K and $0.2$ K
following 171.7 minutes on-source integration time

pi_or_archival_as_stated.value: PI E. F. van Dishoeck; PILS continuum taken from ALMA archive

evidence.quote: We took the continuum image of the PILS survey at $\nu {\sim}348.815$ GHz from the ALMA archive

provided.value: Band 7 column densities and continuum image for comparison

evidence.quote: We took the continuum image of the PILS survey at $\nu {\sim}348.815$ GHz from the ALMA archive

what.value: PILS Band 7 column densities of many species

evidence.quote: The column densities of PILS are taken from (cite: Coutens2016) (NH$_2$CHO)

external_data_from_literature.citation: Coutens2016; Jorgensen2016; Calcutt2018; Jorgensen2018; Persson2018; Manigand2020; Drozdovskaya2022; Ilyushin2022; Drozdovskaya2018; Ferrer2023; Lykke2017

evidence.quote: scaling the $^{13}$CH$_3$OH column density by $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C $= 68$ ((cite: Milam2005))

what.value: Dust temperature range / inner region ~90 K

evidence.quote: The temperature of the inner regions based on models of (cite: Jacobsen2018) is ${\sim} 90$ K.

pipeline_or_manual.value: CASA pipeline, then self-calibrated with CASA

evidence.quote: calibrated with the CASA pipeline ((cite: McMullin2007)) and then self-calibrated with CASA
Continuum subtraction was done on the self-calibrated image datacubes using STATCONT ((cite: Sanchez2018)).
For more information on the data calibration, reduction and imaging, as well as first results on gas accretion flow in the IRAS16293 system see (cite: Murillo2022)

what.value: Fit-by-eye LTE fitting and uncertainty estimate

evidence.quote: The fitting followed a similar procedure as the fit-by-eye method used in (cite: Nazari2022ALMAGAL).

what.value: Extraction position 0.5'' offset from continuum peak

evidence.quote: extracted from the same $0.5\ensuremath{''}$ offset position from the continuum peak of B that was used in many of the works from ALMA-PILS

unstated_but_needed: Imaging parameters (weighting, robust, cell, image size, tclean settings) not given
Self-calibration solution intervals and CASA version for reduction
Exact definition of the 1'' beam used for column densities
Detailed procedure for the column density uncertainties and upper limits

method.value: Spectrum extracted at 0.5'' offset position from continuum peak of B

evidence.quote: The spectrum of IRAS16293 B (Fig. [1](#fig:overview)) was extracted from the same $0.5\ensuremath{''}$ offset position from the continuum peak of B

analysis_steps.goal: LTE fit of column densities and Tex

method.value: CASSIS LTE modelling varying N and Tex by eye; all lines of a molecule fitted simultaneously; detection if >=3 lines at >=3 sigma

evidence.quote: We consider a molecule as detected if it has at least three lines at a peak of $\geq3\sigma$ level.

key_parameters.value: FWHM fitted on unblended lines then fixed (~1.8±0.5 km/s); Tex fitted only if >=2 lines with range of Eup, else fixed to 100 K (300 K for t-HCOOH, NH2CHO)

evidence.quote: If not enough lines with a range of $E_{\rm up}$ were detected, the temperature is fixed to 100 K
the source velocity was fixed to $V_{\rm lsr} = 2.7$ km s$^{-1}$

assumptions.value: LTE, beam dilution of unity (source fills ~1'' beam)

evidence.quote: a beam dilution of unity was assumed resulting in our column densities being representative of those within a beam

fitting.value: Fit by eye; typical column density uncertainty ~20%

evidence.quote: the typical uncertainty from the fits is on the order of 20$\%$
the rest of the lines are explained reasonably well (i.e., within ${\sim}20-30\%$

method.value: Model upper limits with Tex fixed to 100 K and FWHM to 2 km/s

evidence.quote: The upper limits are measured by fixing $T_{\rm ex}$ to 100 K and FWHM to 2 km s$^{-1}$.

method.value: tau = -ln(1 - F/(Omega B(Tdust))) at Band 3 and PILS Band 7 continuum, at peak and offset position, over a range of Tdust

evidence.quote: Next, we calculated $\tau_{\rm dust}$ for a range of dust temperatures that are feasible for IRAS16293B
The temperature of the inner regions based on models of (cite: Jacobsen2018) is ${\sim} 90$ K.

method.value: Correct PILS column densities by beam dilution factor 0.5, compare N and N/N(CH3OH) between bands

evidence.quote: The PILS column densities are converted to an average over the PILS beam (or filling the PILS beam uniformly) by multiplication with their beam dilution factor

validation.value: CH3COOH refit in Band 7 with new spectroscopy

evidence.quote: we re-did the fit to CH$_3$COOH in the Band 7 data using new spectroscopic data

used_for.value: Calibration pipeline, self-calibration, continuum flux measurement

evidence.quote: For this measurement we used CASA ((cite: McMullin2007)) version 6.5.2.26
Continuum subtraction was done on the self-calibrated image datacubes using STATCONT

used_for.value: Line identification and LTE spectral fitting

evidence.quote: we identified as many molecules as possible using the CASSIS[^1] spectral analysis tool
The line lists were taken from the CDMS ((cite: Muller2001); (cite: Muller2005)) or the JPL database ((cite: Pickett1998)).
The line density of the lines detected at $\gtrsim 6\sigma$ level in Band 3 (${\sim}100$ GHz) data is 1 per ${\sim}8.5$ MHz
is found to be $8.2 \times 10^{18}$ cm$^{-2}$ in the ${\sim}1\ensuremath{''}$ beam

results_numeric.quantity: Optical depth at offset position (Band 3 and Band 7)

evidence.quote: the dust optical depth for the PILS continuum is almost the same as that of Band 3 which is ${\sim}0.15$

results_numeric.quantity: Scatter of Band 3 vs Band 7 column densities

evidence.quote: the scatter around the line of $N_{\rm Band 3} = N_{\rm Band 7}$ is a factor of 1.9 below the line and 1.8 above the line

findings_qualitative.value: No glycerol, i- or n-propanol detected; 31 species detected (~15 tentative); ~25-30% of >=6 sigma lines unidentified

evidence.quote: We do not detect glycerol or i- and n-propanol but provide upper limits for them

claims.hypothesis: Band 3 spectra are much less line-confused than Band 7
claims.result: 1 line per 8.5 MHz vs 1 per 3.5 MHz
claims.finding: Line density only ~2.5 times lower; spectrum remains crowded

evidence.quote: The line density in Band 3 is only ${\sim}2.5$ times lower in frequency space than in Band 7.

claims.hypothesis: Larger COMs (glycerol, propanols) are detectable at 3 mm
claims.experiment: Fit LTE models, derive upper limits
claims.result: Non-detections with limits consistent with lab studies
claims.finding: 3 mm has not yet yielded larger molecules in warm sources

evidence.quote: The 3 mm search has not yet resulted in detection of larger and more complex molecules in warm sources.

claims.hypothesis: Dust optical depth affects column densities and ratios between bands
claims.experiment: Compare Band 3 and PILS Band 7 values at offset position
claims.finding: Dust optical depth effect is minimal at off-source location

evidence.quote: We conclude that around IRAS16293 B dust optical depth does not affect the column densities and the ratios of various molecules

why_this_data.value: Settings optimized for glycerol and propanols; lower line confusion expected at 3 mm

evidence.quote: This data set was specifically taken to search for large species due to the expected lower line density and line confusion in Band 3

limitations_admitted.value: Single/limited lines for some species; coarse spectral resolution; low angular resolution; upper limits depend on assumed Tex and lines covered

evidence.quote: given that the upper limits reported here depend on the assumed excitation temperature and more importantly the lines covered in our data

referee_caveats_inferred: Fit-by-eye fitting without a formal likelihood or sampler
Beam dilution of unity ignores differing emitting areas
Single offset position cannot test on-source dust attenuation

data_public_as_stated.value: Project codes given; PILS continuum from ALMA archive

evidence.quote: We took the continuum image of the PILS survey at $\nu {\sim}348.815$ GHz from the ALMA archive

missing_for_reproduction: Fit-by-eye procedure details and uncertainty method (only referenced)
reproducibility.score_reason: Public data and a tabulated results set, but imaging/calibration details are deferred to another paper and fitting is by eye.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Fit-by-eye procedure and missing reduction details make exact reproduction hard.
